name: Cinnamon Bay
description: The longest beach in Virgin Islands National Park, with room to spread out, a campground next door, watersports access, and snorkeling around Cinnamon Cay.
accessNotes: North Shore Road reaches the beach and campground area.
Arrive early because parking at popular north-shore beaches is limited.
safetyNotes: There is no lifeguard on duty; check water and weather conditions before entering.
parking: Limited national-park parking; popular lots can fill by 10 a.m.
accessibility: Accessible paths are available through the campground area.

name: Francis Bay
description: A long St. John beach known for calmer swimming, beginner-friendly snorkeling, turtle sightings, and the bird-rich Francis Bay trail and pond.
accessNotes: Vehicle access and parking are available near the beach.
Pair the beach with the quarter-mile pond trail for wildlife viewing.
safetyNotes: There is no lifeguard on duty; north swells can reduce visibility.
parking: On-site parking is available but limited during busy periods.

accessNotes: Reach the beach directly from North Shore Road, the closest park beach by road from Cruz Bay.
Parking is limited; safari taxis are often easier on busy days.
safetyNotes: There is no lifeguard on duty; confirm current water conditions.
parking: Small national-park lot; arrive early in peak periods.

name: Magens Bay
description: St. Thomas’s signature mile-long beach park, combining typically calm swimming with full facilities, food, rentals, trails, and easy taxi access.
accessNotes: Pay admission at the entrance or purchase a pass through the Magens Bay Authority.
Taxi service and on-site parking make this one of St. Thomas’s easiest beach days.
safetyNotes: Use the designated swim area and follow posted lifeguard guidance.
fees: Non-residents $7; residents $2 with local ID; children under 12 free; parking $2.
parking: Large paid beach-park lot; $2 per vehicle.
accessibility: Beach wheelchairs and accessible park facilities are available; confirm availability before arrival.

name: Maho Bay
description: A shallow north-shore favorite with a long sandy edge and seagrass habitat where green sea turtles are often seen, especially early or late in the day.
accessNotes: Use the large parking area at the eastern end and never park on vegetation.
The western end has restrooms; the shoreline extends about 0.3 miles.
safetyNotes: Give turtles and other wildlife plenty of space; never touch, chase, or feed them.
There is no lifeguard on duty; north swells can reduce visibility.
parking: Large lot at the eastern end; roadside and vegetation parking are not permitted.

name: Salt Pond Bay
description: A quieter south-shore beach reached by a downhill hike, with snorkeling, a salt pond, and access to the exposed Ram Head trail.
accessNotes: Expect roughly a half-mile downhill walk from the parking area, followed by an uphill return.
Carry drinking water and sturdy shoes if continuing to Ram Head.
safetyNotes: There is no lifeguard; remain alert for boat traffic, wildlife, heat, and changing water conditions.
parking: Limited roadside parking above the access trail.

name: Trunk Bay
description: Virgin Islands National Park’s showcase beach, pairing white sand and clear water with an underwater snorkel trail and the park’s most complete visitor facilities.
hours: Snack shack and bar 10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.
accessNotes: North Shore Road provides direct access; parking is limited and can fill by 10 a.m.
Safari taxis from Cruz Bay are a practical alternative on busy days.
safetyNotes: NPS currently lists no lifeguard on duty; check posted conditions and stay within your ability.
fees: Amenity fee required; confirm the current amount with the National Park Service.
parking: Limited paved lot; arrive early or use a safari taxi.
accessibility: Paved access connects the parking and facility area; contact the park for current accessibility details.
